headline_marked: BMW to launch [[navigation-guided city driving]] in 2027, challenging Tesla FSD
headline: BMW to launch navigation-guided city driving in 2027, challenging Tesla FSD
summary: BMW's new system will assist with steering, speed, and lane changes on city streets, requiring driver supervision as a Level 2 system.
details: BMW announced it will introduce navigation-guided, partially automated driving capabilities for urban environments starting in 2027. The system will initially launch in Germany, with plans to expand to other markets subsequently.

This new feature will assist drivers with steering, accelerating, and braking on both highways and city streets, utilizing the car's GPS navigation. In urban settings, it will help with lane changes, turns, yielding, and navigating roundabouts. However, it remains a Level 2 driver assist system, mandating that drivers keep their eyes on the road and be ready to intervene at any moment.

While drivers can remove their hands from the wheel on highways, they must keep them on the wheel when using the system on local roads. This move positions BMW as a competitor to Tesla's Full Self-Driving (FSD) system, as the automotive industry accelerates the development of autonomous driving features.

BMW's system is designed to work collaboratively with the driver, allowing for immediate manual control of steering, braking, or acceleration without deactivating the system. The car will provide visual feedback through the heads-up display and a 3D map on the main dashboard, showing what the assistance system perceives and its actions.

Existing models such as the BMW 3 Series, 7 Series, X5, iX3, and iX4 are equipped with the necessary cameras and sensors to support this feature. BMW plans to activate it via over-the-air software updates. The system complies with new European safety regulations that permit automated driving suggestions and actions on city streets.

Despite advancements, safety researchers express concerns about driver attention and the potential for crashes with increasing adoption of Level 2 systems. Studies suggest that many driver-assist systems may be less safe than human driving due to driver overreliance and delayed reaction times when taking back control.

BMW emphasizes that drivers remain responsible for the vehicle even when using the partially autonomous system in cities, similar to Tesla's approach with FSD. This stance is crucial as legal interpretations of responsibility in accidents involving autonomous features continue to evolve.

headline_marked: [[German lawmakers' iPhones]] targeted by mercenary spyware, Apple warns
headline: German lawmakers' iPhones targeted by mercenary spyware, Apple warns
summary: Apple has sent threat notifications to politicians and public figures in Germany, warning of potential mercenary spyware attacks. The BSI advises recipients to assume their devices may be compromised.
details: Germany's federal cybersecurity office (BSI) confirmed that members of the Bundestag and other notable individuals received Apple threat notifications. These alerts warn that their iPhones may have been targeted by sophisticated spyware.

The spyware in question is described as 'mercenary spyware,' often purchased by governments from private vendors. These tools can steal sensitive information like messages and location data, often using 'zero-click' exploits that require no user interaction.

While Apple does not attribute specific attacks or confirm compromise, the BSI urges anyone receiving such a notification to assume their device may have been affected. The threat notifications were sent to users in 99 countries.

The exact perpetrators and their government affiliations remain unclear. However, the incident highlights the growing threat of state-sponsored cyberattacks against civil society and political figures globally.
